title: The symmetric algebra of a finite projective module is smooth
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a finite projective $A$-module (a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module), and $\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ its symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Then the structure map $A\to\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07M6 (lemma-symmetric-algebra-smooth, line 2112), the implication 'M finite projective => Sym_A(M) smooth' (second paragraph of its proof, using Lemma Tag 07EV lemma-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra)

proof.text: Put $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$, an $A$-algebra via the structure map $\alpha:A\to C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] there are $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$ generating the unit ideal such that for every $i$ the localization $M_{f_i}$ is a finite free $A_{f_i}$-module, say $M_{f_i}\cong A_{f_i}^{\oplus n_i}$ with $n_i\ge0$. Write $1=\sum_i a_if_i$ with $a_i\in A$ and put $g_i=\alpha(f_i)\in C$; applying the ring homomorphism $\alpha$ gives $1=\sum_i\alpha(a_i)g_i$, so $g_1,\dots,g_r$ generate the unit ideal of $C$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), (3)$\Rightarrow$(7) (finite projective $\Rightarrow$ finite locally free, Definition Tag 00NV)

proof.text: Fix $i$ and write $f=f_i$, $g=g_i$, $n=n_i$. The localization $C_g$ of $C$ at the powers of $g=\alpha(f)$ is, as an $A_f$-algebra, $A_f\otimes_AC$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] (first assertion, with $R=A$ and the $A$-algebra $C$), and by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] (with $R\to S$ the map $A\to A_f$) the $A_f$-algebra $A_f\otimes_AC$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Sym}_{A_f}(A_f\otimes_AM)$; finally $A_f\otimes_AM\cong M_f$ as $A_f$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] (second assertion). So $C_g\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{A_f}(M_f)$ as $A_f$-algebras, the $A$-algebra structure of $C_g$ being $A\to C\to C_g$, which is also $A\to A_f\to C_g$ since all the isomorphisms are $A_f$-linear and send $1$ to $1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0C6F (lemma-tensor-algebra-localization: $\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)_f=\operatorname{Sym}_{A_f}(M_f)$) and Lemma Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization)

proof.text: An $A_f$-linear isomorphism $u:M_f\to A_f^{\oplus n}$ induces an isomorphism of $A_f$-algebras $\operatorname{Sym}_{A_f}(M_f)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{A_f}(A_f^{\oplus n})$: by the universal property [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] $\iota\circ u$ and $\iota\circ u^{-1}$ extend to $A_f$-algebra maps $U$, $U'$ in the two directions, and $U'\circ U$ and $U\circ U'$ agree with the identity on the image of $\iota$, hence are the identity by the uniqueness clause. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] $\operatorname{Sym}_{A_f}(A_f^{\oplus n})\cong A_f[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ as $A_f$-algebras. With the previous step, $C_g\cong A_f[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ as $A_f$-algebras, hence as $A$-algebras (both via $A\to A_f$).

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra): $\operatorname{Sym}$ of a finite free module is a polynomial algebra

proof.text: $A\to C_g$ is smooth. The map $A\to A$ (the identity) is smooth, being the polynomial ring in $0$ variables [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]; hence $A\to A_f$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization] (with $R=S=A$ and $g=f$). The map $A_f\to A_f[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], so the composite $A\to A_f\to A_f[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (2). By the previous step $C_g$ is isomorphic to this $A$-algebra, and smoothness [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] is invariant under isomorphisms of $A$-algebras (finite presentation, $H_1(L_{-/A})$ and $\Omega_{-/A}$ are carried along by an isomorphism of $A$-algebras), so $A\to C_g$ is smooth.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 00T6 and Lemma Tag 00T7 (polynomial algebras are standard smooth, hence smooth), Lemma Tag 00T3 (lemma-localize-smooth), Lemma Tag 00TD (lemma-compose-smooth)

proof.text: So $A\to C_{g_i}$ is smooth for every $i$, and $g_1,\dots,g_r$ generate the unit ideal of $C$ (first step). By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-local-on-cover] (with $R=A$, $S=C$), $A\to C=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ is smooth.
